bug_semantics: ChaiScript's built-in async() launched a script closure with std::async(std::launch::async, ...) but did not make the Dispatch_Engine own or join the worker. During engine teardown, an outstanding script worker could continue formatting an eval_error and call Dispatch_Engine::get_type_name and Type_Info::bare_equal while the main thread destroyed the engine's type maps, producing a race-dependent heap use-after-free.
flaw_origin: Commit 52d03a66b15358e8fd2caeb5b063044c8aa839d2 first registered async() in include/chaiscript/chaiscript_stdlib.hpp as a bare std::async launch and returned only its future; it added no engine-lifetime tracking or teardown synchronization. That single addition created the vulnerable cross-thread lifetime relationship. Later edits only adjusted registration syntax, module passing, namespaces, or formatting while retaining the same untracked launch.
ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object names author Jason Turner <jason@emptycrate.com> and committer Jason Turner <jason@emptycrate.com>; its complete message is 'Add future support, and fix returning of r-values' and has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
evidence: First-party issue https://github.com/ChaiScript/ChaiScript/issues/636 documents the ASan UAF path: an async worker formatting eval_error calls include/chaiscript/dispatchkit/dispatchkit.hpp get_type_name and include/chaiscript/dispatchkit/type_info.hpp Type_Info::bare_equal after the main thread frees the type-map node; the maintainer closed it as fixed by PR https://github.com/ChaiScript/ChaiScript/pull/656. In the validated full-history clone, `git log -L 50,56:include/chaiscript/chaiscript_stdlib.hpp 1b27d0dd15f45b4781273bc039713a8d8608cf86` follows the vulnerable std::async line through formatting/registration-only commits and ends at 52d03a66b15358e8fd2caeb5b063044c8aa839d2. Narrow `git log --reverse -S 'std::async(std::launch::async' -- include/chaiscript/chaiscript_stdlib.hpp` reports exactly the 2015 addition 52d03a66b15358e8fd2caeb5b063044c8aa839d2 and the 2026 removal 7b95ff5126f0365c101b08fa33b50ae387342484. `git show 52d03a66b15358e8fd2caeb5b063044c8aa839d2` shows the BIC adding future registration plus `async`, whose lambda directly returns `std::async(std::launch::async, t_func)`. Direct parent-tree inspection with `git show a32a180a063d9186ca38b2708a9c19d50da378db:include/chaiscript/chaiscript_stdlib.hpp` shows the file exists but has neither <future>, future registration, async registration, nor std::async, proving immediate-parent absence. The BIC's own unittests/future.chai demonstrates four script functions launched through async(), confirming the feature's intended attack-relevant path. Version checks show v5.5.1 (commit 7478d5726425e725e1dd1a7c60f2059f55fab795) lacks the mechanism, v5.5.1..v5.6.0 contains the BIC, `git describe --contains` places it at tags/v5.6.0~12, and `git tag --contains` lists every release v5.6.0 through v6.1.0, matching the advisory's upper affected boundary. Fix commit 7b95ff5126f0365c101b08fa33b50ae387342484 is a one-parent direct source fix on develop after v6.1.0: it removes the raw std::async registration, makes Dispatch_Engine track spawned std::threads, and joins them in its destructor before shared state is destroyed; its regression test explicitly destroys an engine while async work remains. No release tag in the clone contains the fix, so the first patched boundary in public history is that develop commit rather than a tagged release. Finally, `git cat-file commit 52d03a66b15358e8fd2caeb5b063044c8aa839d2` supplies the BIC-only identity/message evidence quoted in ai_marker.
reasoning: The advisory's crashing instruction is Type_Info::bare_equal, but that comparison did not create the lifetime violation; it is merely where the async worker dereferenced already-freed engine-owned type data. The causal root is the first public async entry point that allowed engine-dependent script work to outlive engine storage. The -L trace distinguishes 52d03a66b15358e8fd2caeb5b063044c8aa839d2 from later moves/refactors, while the -S result brackets the mechanism from its addition to the direct fix. The immediate parent contains the standard library without any future/async facility, whereas the BIC adds the untracked forced-async launch in one regular, non-squash commit; therefore it is the smallest real BIC and parent absence is directly proven. Tag ancestry establishes introduction in v5.6.0, persistence through the advisory's v6.1.0 upper bound, and remediation only in later untagged develop history. PR #656 fixes the same lifecycle defect by transferring thread ownership to Dispatch_Engine and joining before teardown, validating the causal choice. Although the fixing commit is explicitly AI-assisted, the protocol attributes AI only from the BIC commit object. The 2015 BIC has a human author and committer and no AI marker or trailer, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
